newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-LATE GOALS SAVE GHANA'S HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE GOALS SAVE GHANA'S HOPES.

text.p: Two late goals handed Ghana a World Cup lifeline as they came from behind to draw with Morocco on a dramatic weekend of qualifiers in Africa.
Sam Johnson and Arthur Moses, both based in Europe, both scored in the last five minutes to bring Ghana back from a potentially crippling defeat on Sunday at home in Kumasi to the Moroccans.
But the 2-2 draw was still a bitter blow to Ghana's hopes of a first-ever appearance in the World Cup finals.
They was also a surprise draw on Sunday for Nigeria, who were held by Kenya in Nairobi, and for Zaire and Cameroon, who dropped valuable home points in their respective groups.
Guinea, Sierra Leone, Tunisia and Zimbabwe were the only teams to record victories in the 10 matches played on the weekend.

Ghana, who have the best record in African competition but have never qualified for the World Cup finals, found themselves two goals down with 10 minutes to go after Morocco scored through Saleheddine Bassir and Sporting Lisbon's Mustpaha Hadji.
Johnson, who plays for Belgian club Anderlecht, pulled one back for Ghana with five minutes left to set up a dramatic finale which saw Moses hammer home a freekick for the equaliser in injury-time.
Nigeria also came from behind against Kenya to force a 1-1 draw on Sunday with German-based Jonathan Akpoborie scoring his first international goal.
The youthful Kenyan team had taken the lead after 25 minutes through Ken Simiyu.
The draw handed the lead in group one to Guinea after their 2-0 away victory over Burkina Faso in Ouagadougou on Sunday.
First half-goals from Souleymane Oulare and Momo Wandel Soumah mean Guinea have a 100 percent record after their opening two qualifiers.
Tunisia are the only other team to have won both their qualifiers, going to the top of group two with a 1-0 win over Egypt at home on Sunday.
Zoubier Beya scored after 10 minutes but the Tunisians might have won by a greater margin had they used chances that came their way.
Cameroon, Zaire and Zambia are received setbacks after being held to draws at home.
Cameroon drew 0-0 with Angola in Yaounde in group four while Zambia lost valuable ground to South Africa in group three after their goalless draw in Lusaka on Saturday.

Zaire conceded a surprise goal to Congo after just three minutes in Kinshasa on Sunday and although Belgian-based fullback Nzelo Lembi equaliser 10 minutes later, they failed to beat their unfancied neighbours.
Zimbabwe's 3-0 win over Togo in Harare in group four on Sunday was the biggest win of the weekend with Vitalis Takawira scoring twice.
Abu Kanu's goal gave Sierra Leone a narrow 1-0 home win over Gabon while Liberia, playing without any of their European-based professionals, drew 0-0 away in Namibia.
The Liberian team, whose trip was again partly funded by AC Milan's George Weah, received pre-match instruction from the Weah on the telephone.
Weah missed the match through injury.
